items.title: USDY: Treasuries That Pay Yield Onchain
items.summary: Over $28 trillion sits in US Treasury notes and almost none of it has touched a public network. Tokenization is changing that, producing a new asset class that generates yield rather than holding a flat peg. Ondo calls it a yieldcoin. Ondo Finance's USDY is a tokenized note backed by short-term US Treasuries and bank demand deposits, earning yield automatically reflected in the token itself. Investors hold a real income-producing asset directly in their wallet. Unlike a stablecoin pegged to stay flat, USDY tracks the value of what backs it. It has since grown to around $2.1 billion in assets across six networks, with Solana among its fastest-growing deployments. Originally produced in May 2025. Some details may have changed since. Ondo Finance: https://ondo.finance USDY: https://ondo.finance/usdy X: @OndoFinance: https://x.com/OndoFinance solana.com: Overview of Institutional Real World Assets on Solana: https://solana.com/news/overview-of-institutional-real-world-assets-on-solana ("USDY is a tokenized note backed by short-term U.S. Treasuries and bank demand deposits") Nathan Allman on Talking Tokens: https://solana.com/podcasts/talking-tokens/episodes/nathan-allman-is-2025-the-year-everything-gets-tokenized-e327hss

items.title: Show HN: ChainBounty – improving the blockchain funding model
items.summary: Abstract. Token-funded bounties to incentivize competition-style participation in blockchain development projects would result in wider and better allocation of investment, and allow investors to diversify exposure across a field of potentially successful projects. Overall this would increase the rate of progress within development of the blockchain space. We propose a centralised platform for the administration of token-funded bounty driven development projects whereby experts allocate pools of invested capital according to the technical merits of development projects, and investors are rewarded with token allocation in funded projects. Draft Whitepaper: http://chainbounty.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/chainbount... We see this as bringing a variation of the YC model to blockchain - experts select large numbers of small projects and provide them with funding to reach the next level of development. This is in contrast to heavily funded ICOs where tiny teams of developers are given hundreds of millions of dollars. After feedback from HN readers: - Do you think this model will better incentivize development in the blockchain space? - What particular challenges do you think would be useful to run? https://twitter.com/ChainBounty/ https://www.facebook.com/ChainBounty-449553402088106/

items.title: The Praxian Genocidal Kill Chain — Part 3
items.summary: Download PDF The Praxians—a new breed of tech billionaires—form the core of the Silicon Valley-rooted wing of the global oligarchy. The Praxians are a subset of the network of tech moguls who are embedded within and encircle the Trump administration. The Praxians are distinguished by their close affiliation with the ideas of the Neoreactionary movement (NRx) and by their enthusiasm for building their own private city-states. Some Praxians, such as Marc Andreessen, openly declare their adherence to NRx principles. Others, such as Mark Zuckerberg, extol NRx ideology through their corporate sloganeering. And still others, such as Peter Thiel, continuously fund specific NRx projects, such as Praxis in Greenland (see Part 1). Ironically, there are aspects of the technology that the Praxians are encouraging us to adopt for their own ends that we could instead repurpose to finally free ourselves from their hierarchical authoritarianism. We could flip the features of programmable digital currency , such as central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) or stablecoins, and turn them from the ideal tool for centralised control into the means by which we achieve monetary and economic emancipation. And we could use some facets of the network state —the Praxians’ own technology-based nation-building strategy—to construct new models of sovereign decentralised sociopolitical structures.
